overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance clearly indicates that high-concept space and extreme 'What If' planetary scenarios are dramatically outperforming standard trivia or psychology facts in both views-per-day and engagement (likes/comments per view). Videos featuring bizarre planetary mechanics, extreme physics, and hypothetical immersion scenarios (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') achieve up to 1,024+ views rapidly, whereas standard brain or animal facts lag significantly behind. Engagement is heavily concentrated on immersive, visually descriptive space anomalies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generated over 1,000 views and exceptionally high likes (38+) within days.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space disaster/immersion scenarios involving extreme planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing impossible weather or dark matter ('The Planet Darker Than Coal', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies') drive strong organic reach and active comment engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain high focus on weird space phenomena, focusing on sensory extremes like supersonic rains, total darkness, or extreme temperatures.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal human psychology and brain tricks ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') stalled out below 60-70 views with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia and internal brain hacks in favor of external, awe-inspiring physical science and space concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' underperformed relative to cosmic scale content, showing lower viewer velocity outside of rare outliers.
weak_patterns.action: Limit standard animal trivia unless tied to a cinematic survival or extreme 'What If' narrative.
